Click on the gear symbol, Look for "subtitles/CC", and toggle on. You may need to change language. Note that there're sometimes both auto-generated English as well as English uploaded by the channel owner.
You can also press "c" on your keyboard to toggle "subtitles/CC" on or off.

comments.author: @EpicEarthYTB
comments.text: It’s truly mind-blowing how these structures have stood the test of time. They are a powerful testament to the limits of human ingenuity.

replies.author: @trueglobe66
replies.text: Absolutely! It’s incredible to think that many of these structures were created centuries ago with tools far simpler than what we have today. Which masterpiece in the documentary impressed you most, and was it the scale, engineering, or sheer difficulty of building it that amazed you?

comments.author: @Aventurex-686
comments.text: Watching this documentary feels like flipping through humanity's greatest highlight reel. Every masterpiece quietly says, "Someone once thought this was impossible." Meanwhile, I celebrate when I successfully assemble a bookshelf without reading the instructions twice. Which creation deserves to be called humanity's greatest achievement?

replies.author: @trueglobe66
replies.text: That bookshelf comparison made us smile! 😄 It really is amazing how often humanity has turned “impossible” into something that still stands centuries later. Which structure in the documentary made you wonder most, “How did they actually build this with the technology they had?”

comments.author: @unknownplanetdoc
comments.text: The deeper I got into this video, the more I kept wondering how many masterpieces like these have disappeared without us ever knowing they existed

replies.author: @trueglobe66
replies.text: That’s such a fascinating thought. It makes you wonder how many extraordinary structures have been lost to time before anyone had the chance to document them. Which kind of lost masterpiece would you most want archaeologists to discover today—an ancient city, a temple, or something completely unexpected?

comments.author: @TravelUncovered68
comments.text: What amazes me most is how these structures survived so much history. Human creativity really can leave a mark that lasts for generations.
